\chapter{Detailed Requirements}\label{app:requirements}

\section{Detailed Use Cases}\label{appb:sec:usecases}
Full templates for the seven use cases summarised in Table \ref{ch4:tab:usecases} and Figure
\ref{ch4:fig:usecases}. A note on sequencing: the diagram's \texttt{<<include>>} chain
(UC1~$\to$~UC2~$\to$~UC3~$\to$~UC4~$\to$~UC5~$\to$~UC6) is a \textbf{capability decomposition}
--- the standard UML reading of \texttt{<<include>>} (``achieving UC1 requires UC2, which
requires UC3, \ldots'') --- not a claim about execution order. The \textbf{Main Flow} below each
use case states the real order, taken directly from \texttt{runner/diagnose.py} and
\texttt{runner/cli.py}: UC3 (resource evidence) actually runs \emph{after} UC4 (search) finds a
candidate, not before it, because only a found polluter has anything for UC3 to analyse. This is
disclosed here rather than left as a silent mismatch between the diagram and the real pipeline.

\subsection*{UC1: Submit Diagnosis Request}
\textbf{Actor:} Developer, CI Pipeline. \quad \textbf{Traces to:} FR-1.

\textbf{Preconditions:} the target Maven module is checked out at a pinned commit; a target
test is known to fail; JDK~8+ and Maven are on \texttt{PATH}.

\textbf{Main Flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item The actor invokes \texttt{py -m runner diagnose --project DIR --victim Class\#method}
    (optionally \texttt{--n}, \texttt{--records}, \texttt{--order}, \texttt{--shuffles},
    \texttt{--seed} --- \texttt{runner/cli.py}).
  \item The CLI validates \texttt{--victim} is \texttt{Class\#method} and that
    \texttt{DIR/pom.xml} exists.
  \item Control passes to UC2 (\texttt{runner.diagnose.diagnose()}).
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Postconditions:} a \texttt{DiagnosisRuns} run is underway, or the request was rejected.

\textbf{Exceptions:} a malformed \texttt{--victim} or missing \texttt{pom.xml} exits 2 (input
error) before any test is run.

\subsection*{UC2: Run Ordered Test Replay}
\textbf{Actor:} (included by UC1). \quad \textbf{Traces to:} FR-2.

\textbf{Preconditions:} UC1 validated; the project compiles under Maven.

\textbf{Main Flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item The source tree is hashed (SHA-256) for the later integrity check.
  \item \texttt{discover\_order()} lists every test method in the module, alphabetical by
    class (Surefire's default), unless \texttt{--order} supplied an explicit order.
  \item That order runs \texttt{n} times (default 20), one fresh JVM per run
    (\texttt{runner/order\_runner.py}).
  \item If it never reproduces the failure, up to \texttt{--shuffles} (default 31) distinct,
    class-grouped shuffled orders are tried (ADR-008) until one reproduces or the budget is
    exhausted.
  \item The victim is run alone \texttt{n} times regardless of the above, to check it does not
    simply fail by itself.
  \item Control passes to UC4.
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Postconditions:} a reference failure signature is captured, or the run is established as
genuinely \texttt{NOT\_REPRODUCED}.

\textbf{Exceptions:} a JVM crash or timeout is recorded as an infrastructure failure
(\texttt{infrastructure\_failures}, ADR-008) and reported as such --- never silently dropped
and never counted as a pass.

\subsection*{UC3: Collect Resource Evidence}
\textbf{Actor:} (included by UC1; in the real pipeline, triggered after UC4 --- see the note
above). \quad \textbf{Traces to:} FR-3.

\textbf{Preconditions:} UC4 found at least one candidate polluter (status
\texttt{POLLUTER\_FOUND}). If it did not, UC3 does not run.

\textbf{Main Flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item For each polluter UC4/UC5 identified, \texttt{evidence.extract.analyse\_pair()} reads
    the polluter's and victim's compiled bytecode with \texttt{javap} (no source is read, no
    code is instrumented or modified --- ADR-001).
  \item It walks call sites for \texttt{getstatic}/\texttt{putstatic} and
    \texttt{System.setProperty}/\texttt{getProperty}, starting at depth 2 and auto-deepening one
    level at a time (1--5) only if nothing is found (ADR-006).
  \item With more than one polluter, \texttt{combine\_fields()} shows the first polluter's edge
    and names the others in \texttt{limitations} --- but only if every polluter has an edge
    (ADR-007); otherwise no single resource is shown as primary.
  \item Control passes to UC6.
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Postconditions:} a shared resource (or \texttt{null}) with bytecode-offset write/read
locations on both sides.

\textbf{Exceptions:} no edge found $\to$ \texttt{NO\_SUPPORTED\_RESOURCE\_EVIDENCE} once UC6
evaluates it; this is not an error, it is a legitimate, typed outcome.

\subsection*{UC4: Search for Polluter}
\textbf{Actor:} (included by UC1). \quad \textbf{Traces to:} FR-4.

\textbf{Preconditions:} UC2 completed; the victim did not fail alone.

\textbf{Main Flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \texttt{find\_polluter()} (\texttt{runner/search.py}) tries each candidate test
    one-by-one, immediately before the victim, stopping at the first that reproduces the
    reference signature (ranked one-by-one policy, FR-4).
  \item If none reproduces it alone, the run is \texttt{NO\_SINGLE\_POLLUTER} and control passes
    to UC5's minimisation step instead.
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Postconditions:} either a single polluter is identified, or the status is
\texttt{NO\_SINGLE\_POLLUTER}, which UC5 may still resolve.

\textbf{Exceptions:} the cost-aware adaptive policy FR-4 also commits to is \textbf{not built}
--- see Table \ref{ch4:tab:fr}.

\subsection*{UC5: Minimise \& Verify Sequence}
\textbf{Actor:} (included by UC1). \quad \textbf{Traces to:} FR-5.

\textbf{Preconditions:} UC4 found a single polluter, or the failing order has more than one
untried predecessor left to minimise.

\textbf{Main Flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item If UC4 did not find a single polluter, \texttt{ddmin()} (\texttt{runner/minimise.py},
    ADR-007) deletion-minimises the prefix before the victim to a 1-minimal set --- the
    smallest subset that still reproduces, never claimed to be the global minimum.
  \item The resulting sequence (one or more polluters + victim) is replayed \texttt{n} times in
    a fresh JVM each time; successes and any-signature failures are both counted.
  \item \texttt{eval.stats.wilson\_interval()} turns that count into a Wilson 95\% confidence
    interval (tested against \texttt{statsmodels}).
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Postconditions:} a reduced sequence with a measured reproduction rate and interval.

\textbf{Exceptions:} every replay crashing/timing out, never a real exception, is
\texttt{INFRASTRUCTURE\_FAILURE} rather than being folded into the reproduction rate as if it
were a clean pass or a signature mismatch.

\subsection*{UC6: Receive Certificate}
\textbf{Actor:} Developer, CI Pipeline (receives the result of UC1). \quad \textbf{Traces to:}
FR-6.

\textbf{Preconditions:} UC2, (UC4, UC5 as applicable) and UC3 have all run.

\textbf{Main Flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \texttt{eval.outcome.decide()} applies the decision table (Figure
    \ref{ch5:fig:outcome}) to the raw counts and the resource edge, first match wins.
  \item \texttt{eval.report.assemble\_report()} builds the full certificate: victim, polluters,
    reduced sequence, reproduction statistics, resource evidence, failure signature, outcome,
    typed reason, limitations.
  \item \texttt{eval.schema\_validator.validate\_report()} validates it against
    \texttt{eval/schema/report.schema.json} before it is written --- an invalid report is never
    emitted.
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Postconditions:} a schema-valid JSON certificate is written next to its execution
record.

\textbf{Exceptions:} \textbf{the certificate has no literal replay-command field} (Table
\ref{ch4:tab:fr}, FR-6) --- a real, undischarged gap, not an oversight hidden here.

\subsection*{UC7: Invoke via CLI, Consume Exit Code}
\textbf{Actor:} Developer, CI Pipeline. \quad \textbf{Traces to:} FR-7.

\textbf{Preconditions:} none beyond UC1's.

\textbf{Main Flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item The CLI returns exit 0 with the report path printed, once UC6 completes.
  \item If UC6's status cannot be turned into a report yet (\texttt{NO\_SINGLE\_POLLUTER}), the
    CLI prints why and exits 3, rather than emitting a guessed report.
  \item Tool failures (Maven/JDK not found, a crashed subprocess) exit 1; input errors exit 2.
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Postconditions:} the actor (a human or a CI job) can branch on the exit code without
parsing output.

\textbf{Exceptions:} NFR-2's clean-Linux, third-party-verified install is
\textbf{not attempted} in Iteration 1 (Table \ref{ch4:tab:fr}).

\section{Extended Non-Functional Tables}\label{appb:sec:nfr}
This section extends Section \ref{ch4:sec:nfr}'s summary with the full security requirements
table and success-criteria table from \texttt{docs/02-Requirements/non-functional.md}, each
with an Iteration-1 status checked against the real code rather than copied unchanged.

\subsection*{Security requirements}
Every row below describes the \textbf{committed} execution environment for the project as a
whole, not what Iteration 1 runs today. Checked by grepping \texttt{runner/}, \texttt{evidence/}
and \texttt{eval/} for container, sandbox and redaction code: \textbf{none exists yet}.
Iteration 1 runs the analysed project's real tests as a native JVM process on the host machine
(\texttt{runner/order\_runner.py}) --- every row except Audit is therefore a later iteration's
scope (\texttt{docs/00-Meta/roadmap.md} places container/CI security in Iteration 3), stated
plainly rather than implied as already satisfied.

\toprule

\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
\textbf{Requirement} & \textbf{Detail} & \textbf{Status} \\
\midrule

Container & Rootless; no Docker socket mounted; Linux capabilities dropped; no privileged mode &
  Not built --- a later iteration \\
Network & Disabled by default; allowlisted dependency-fetch stage separated from test execution
  & Not built --- a later iteration \\
Limits & CPU, memory, PID, file-size and wall-time; process-group termination; verified cleanup

Audit & Every command, image digest, input commit and environment variable & \textbf{Partial.}
  Every execution record already captures the analysed project's git commit, whether it had

  \texttt{runner.diagnose.environment()}). Image digest: not applicable yet (no container);
  full environment-variable audit: not built. \\

\section{Frozen Definitions Reference}\label{appb:sec:frozen}
\texttt{functional.md} states its own FRs are ``meaningless without'' these definitions, frozen
in version control \emph{before} the first experiment ran. Reproduced here in summary for a
reader who does not have \texttt{docs/02-Requirements/functional.md} open:

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Candidate set.} Every test method in the victim's Maven module except the
    victim itself. A module over 300 such methods is capped to the victim's own package, and
    the cap is declared as a limitation, not hidden.
  \item \textbf{Order-dependent (polluter).} Candidate $c$ such that running $[c, v]$ in one JVM
    reproduces victim $v$'s target failure, while $[v]$ alone passes.
  \item \textbf{Failure signature.} (Exception class, normalised first line of the message,
    topmost project-package stack frame), with digits, hex addresses, temporary paths and
    timestamps masked. A timeout, compile error or out-of-memory is explicitly \textbf{not} the
    same reproduction as the real target assertion failure.
  \item \textbf{Confirmation and cost unit.} One confirmation = one execution of one candidate
    order. Cost is counted in test-method invocations, not Maven launches, since one launch can
    run anywhere from 5 to 5{,}000 tests.
  \item \textbf{Reproduced case.} The victim passes alone in $\geq 10/10$ replays \emph{and}
    fails with the matching signature in $\geq 9/10$ replays of the confirmed polluting order.
  \item \textbf{Resource identifier.} \texttt{ownerInternalName.fieldName:descriptor} for static
    fields only, direct references plus a declared number of hops into project-owned callees.
    Attribution covers the test method, its class's \texttt{setUp}/\texttt{tearDown}, and its
    \texttt{<clinit>}. Reflection, filesystem, system properties (outside the dedicated
    system-property family), network and database state are recorded as
    \textbf{unsupported}, never as zero-overlap --- absence of evidence is not evidence of
    independence.
  \item \textbf{Single-scan protocol.} The exhaustive scan for a case runs exactly once;
    ground truth, every baseline and the ranked strategy are all computed offline from that one
    outcome table. No strategy triggers a re-run of the scan itself.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Amendment, disclosed unprompted (27 August 2026):} execution-context fidelity was added
to the runner definition after the original definition produced false positives on
suite-class-run Surefire configurations. The fix moved a result from 182 false polluters to 0,
\emph{against} the team's own interest (a smaller, more defensible number), and changed neither
the reproduction criterion nor any strategy's scoring. Recorded here exactly as
\texttt{functional.md} records it, because the honesty rule is to volunteer corrections that cut
against your own favour, not just the ones that help it.
